objects.name: Analysis Settings (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects everything OpenSees needs in order to solve - constraint handler, numberer, system of equations, convergence test, solution algorithm, integrator and stepping - into the one object Run Analysis takes.
Every input has a default, so an unconnected component already describes a valid linear static analysis. For a dynamic one set AnalysisType to Transient, and give it a Newmark or Central Difference Integrator, an Analysis Step with Dt, and a Damping.

objects.name: Run Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Writes the assembled model out as an OpenSees script, solves it, and returns the model with its results attached.
Results are recorded to a recorder.mpco file beside the Grasshopper document and read back by the 08_NumericalOutput components; an MPCO Recorder connected to Assemble Model chooses what the file holds, and what it is called. When a run fails the AlpacaModel output comes out empty - read the log output to find out why.

objects.name: Utilisation (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Checks every beam against the design code of its material and reports how much of each resistance it uses: 1 is exactly at the limit.
Steel, to EN 1993-1-1: cross-section class, then axial force, shear, torsion, bending, and bending with axial force and shear (6.2); flexural buckling about both axes (6.3.1); lateral-torsional buckling (6.3.2), with M_cr worked out on each beam's own moment diagram; and bending with compression as a member (6.3.3, by Annex B). Not yet: torsional buckling and Class 4 sections.
The steel grade comes from the beam's material: make it with Material Library Elastic, or name it after its grade ("S355").
One item per beam, in the order of the Element output. A check that could not be made is empty, never zero, and leaves Max empty too.
Fabrication, the partial factors and the report - and the Type, Class and Governing outputs - are in the Design menu below the component.

objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Steel cantilever - the Alpaca4d Utilisation example.

A 4 m cantilever, built in at the root, carries its own weight and 15 kN at the tip. Utilisation checks it to EN 1993-1-1: 1 is exactly at the limit.

The buckling lengths are the point of it. Left empty, Utilisation takes each beam's own length, held at both ends - but a cantilever's tip is free. Here LengthY, LengthZ and LengthLT are twice the length, and the root moment is taken as uniform over it: on the safe side for a root built in sideways and against twist.

HEA 200: bending 0.48, but lateral-torsional buckling 0.89 - LTB governs.
Switch Section to IPE300, the same weight: bending only 0.30, LTB 1.11 - it fails. With the lengths left empty it would have read 0.38.

Open the Report panel to follow the check by hand.
